issues.body: `_approval_reactors_cli()` sorts all unique reactor logins and truncates that untrusted list to the first 50 before the workflow performs any `trust_of` checks. Anyone can react on this public repository, so an attacker can add 50 lexicographically earlier reactor accounts and ensure that a maintainer or write-role reactor sorts after the cap. The workflow then reports `maintainer_approved=0`; on the next content event it restores quarantine even though a valid maintainer approval exists. This is a deterministic public-input denial of the headline durable-approval behavior, and the existing cap test only verifies truncation, not whether a trusted reactor beyond the cap is still honored.
issues.fix_hint: Bound adversary-controlled permission work without discarding authoritative evidence based solely on attacker-controlled sort order. At minimum, recognize/probe the exact trusted maintainer and App identities before applying the general candidate cap; design a bounded strategy for write-role approvals that cannot be crowded out, or explicitly narrow the supported approvers. Add an executed test with more than 50 untrusted reactors and a valid trusted reactor beyond the current sorted prefix, asserting that the approval remains effective.
issues.title: Public reactors can crowd every trusted approval out of the probe cap

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The reaction approval path is generally fail-closed and well exercised, but its public-input probe cap can be exhausted before any trusted reactor is considered. That lets arbitrary users suppress a real maintainer approval and defeats the durability this PR is intended to provide.
